subject: FintechCo - multi-region performance & competitive eval next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo - multi-region performance & competitive eval next steps

Alex - great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Key needs you called out:
- Low tail latency across US, EU, APAC for inference endpoints (especially for fraud-scoring microservice)
- Predictable unit economics / cost controls for high QPS workloads
- Data residency for EU customers and SOC2 evidence for procurement

Where Redwood helps vs hyperscalers (short list):
- Unified inference runtime across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments (so you can start hosted and move to private if needed)
- Cost levers: intelligent batching + quantization profiles we can run per-route for cost/latency tradeoffs
- Smart routing: automated routing to nearest region with fallback to compatible model variants to protect SLOs
- Production-grade observability: token-level cost/latency breakdowns by route + per-model dashboards

Proposed technical next steps:
1) Run a multi-region perf sweep in US (us-west1), EU (europe-west1), APAC (asia-southeast1) for your standard fraud prompts (we can use the sample prompts you mentioned).
2) Include two model variants in the test: an open LLM baseline (e.g., Llama2 13B quantized) and our recommended production variant (quantized + runtime kernels). Compare P95/P99 latency, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens.
3) We'll instrument metrics and share a side-by-side dashboard + short write-up.

Attachments: multi-region-test-plan.md (test cases and execution steps), redwood-vs-hyperscalers-brief.pdf (one-pager comparison)

Questions / asks for you:
- Please share 1-2 representative prompts and expected QPS for the fraud path (approx peak and steady).
- Who should we provision test keys for? (I can provision service accounts for your DevOps team)

Next meeting suggestion: 30-min sync the week of Apr 13 to review initial results.

Thanks - I'll loop Jordan into the perf plan and Sean to help with infra provisioning.

- Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Apr 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo - multi-region performance & competitive eval next steps

Thanks Marissa - helpful recap. A few clarifications:

- For prompts: we can share 3 canonical fraud-check prompts (incl. some short/long variants). Peak QPS for the endpoint is ~1800 sustained for the US and ~600 for EU, APAC each during peak windows.
- Baseline vs hyperscalers: our procurement team specifically asked for a side-by-side P95/P99 compare vs AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex for the same model family. Can Redwood reproduce an equivalent test against those managed inference endpoints, or do you need us to run the hyperscaler side?
- Data residency: we have EU-regulated customers, so we need confirmation that request/response data can be kept in-region or routed to a private deployment. Please add high-level notes in the brief.

I can loop in our DevOps alias for test accounts. If you can send a test plan and an estimate of how long the sweep takes (hours per region), we can prioritize.

- Alex
Head of Platform, FintechCo
alex.chen@fintechco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Apr 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo - multi-region performance & competitive eval next steps

Alex - thanks. Answering inline and attaching a concrete test plan.

On hyperscaler comparison:
- We can run tests from our side for Redwood-hosted endpoints and run parallel synthetic clients against public hyperscaler endpoints (Bedrock, Vertex) to measure network/endpoint differences. For vendor-managed endpoints we will need the model variant name and region from your procurement side (or we can use the publicly available equivalents). If you prefer, we can provide test scripts and you can run the hyperscaler side; either works.

Data residency / private deployment:
- Short answer: yes - we support private deployments (VPC/on-prem) and a customer-managed control plane for EU-only processing. I'll include a short note in the attached brief (redwood-vs-hyperscalers-brief.pdf). For the perf sweep we'll use hosted EU region; if you need strict in-customer-residency tests we can instead spin up our Private evaluation in your EU cloud account (this requires a short setup window).

Estimate for sweep:
- Per region: ~2-3 hours to run the scripted workload for both model variants (includes warmup and KV cache priming). Complete report across 3 regions within 48 hours of test completion.

Attachments: multi-region-test-plan.md (detailed test cases + exact commands), redwood-vs-hyperscalers-brief.pdf (includes data residency notes)

I'll send the test harness and a short checklist for your DevOps team.

- Marissa

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Apr 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: FintechCo - multi-region performance & competitive eval next steps

Looping you both on the plan. Quick internal notes:
- We'll want to ensure we run both 13B quantized and our production 7B/13B optimized kernels (to show cost/latency tradeoffs).
- For EU residency test, prefer to run one sweep using a Private evaluation in FintechCo's EU project if they agree - that gives more accurate e2e residency measurement. Otherwise the hosted eu-west run is fine for latency numbers.
- I'll set up the perf harness on our test runner; need service account for FintechCo DevOps with ephemeral creds.

Jordan Blake
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FintechCo - multi-region performance & competitive eval next steps

Alex / DevOps - thanks for the quick answers. Finalizing next steps and schedule:

1) Test plan & schedule - We'll run the sweep the week of Apr 13. Tentative schedule: us-west1 (Apr 13), europe-west1 (Apr 14), asia-southeast1 (Apr 15). Each region run should take ~3 hours including warmup and cache priming.
2) Model variants - We'll include: (A) quantized 13B baseline, (B) our production-optimized 13B kernel variant, and (C) memory-optimized 13B for cost sensitivity. This will surface P95/P99, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens across each config.
3) What we need from you - 1-3 representative prompts (short + long), an approximate peak QPS window (you provided - thanks), and a DevOps contact to provision an ephemeral service account.
4) Provisioning - Jordan + Sean will provision test runners from our side and can also provide the test scripts for you to run hyperscaler endpoints if you prefer. If you want Redwood to run both sides, please provide model variant names for Bedrock/Vertex or permission to run a public-equivalent config.

Attachments included: multi-region-test-plan.md, redwood-vs-hyperscalers-brief.pdf, test-credentials-instructions.txt

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/98765 (deal), https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cTestPlanLink (test docs)

Can you confirm the DevOps contact and share the prompt set by EOD Apr 10? Once we have that I'll lock the schedule and provision the runs.

Thanks - looking forward to this.
